fr:mainmatter.html:p: Self-host Readeck on macproseph (NixOS) alongside FreshRSS, expose it on the Tailscale interface only, and subscribe FreshRSS to Readeck's per-collection RSS so saved items show up in the reader.

nixpkgs ships both the readeck package (0.21.3) and a services.readeck NixOS module with a hardened systemd unit (DynamicUser, protected filesystem, restricted syscalls). Deployment mirrors the existing freshrss.nix pattern.

html:ul.html:li: Add a new host module hosts/macproseph/readeck.nix enabling services.readeck with settings server.host = "0.0.0.0" and server.port = 8091.
Provide an environmentFile at /mnt/nvme/secrets/readeck.env containing READECK_SECRET_KEY (generated once with openssl rand -hex 32).
Import the new module from configuration.nix.

Open port 8091 on tailscale0 only by adding it to networking.firewall.interfaces.tailscale0.allowedTCPPorts. This matches the FreshRSS pattern — bind to 0.0.0.0 internally, rely on the per-interface firewall for Tailscale-only exposure.
Deploy with nixos-rebuild switch, create the admin account at http://100.83.148.105:8091, and enable the feed token for a "Read Later" collection.

Set up iOS saving via the Readeck PWA "Add to Home Screen" — it registers a Web Share Target, so the iOS share sheet can post into Readeck. (Alternatively, a Shortcuts action posting to /api/bookmarks with an API token.)
Subscribe FreshRSS to the collection's RSS URL and file it under a "Queue" category.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Out of scope for this task: browser extension install on each machine (follow-up), full-text highlight workflow.

fr:title.text: Curate initial feed list in FreshRSS

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Curate initial feed list in FreshRSS

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Populate FreshRSS with an initial set of feeds grouped into coherent categories, then iterate. This is an ongoing task — the first pass should cover the sources already decided on, with later edits expanding into arXiv and academic blogs once those have been thought through.

html:ul.html:li: Queue — Readeck Read-Later feed (http://127.0.0.1:8091/api/bookmarks/feed with HTTP Basic auth, token from Readeck's API tokens page) wired up via sss-009M. Done. YouTube playlist feed (sss-009N) is blocked on YouTube's RSS endpoint situation.
News — Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/rss) and Lobsters (https://lobste.rs/rss) added. Done.
Blogs — TBD. Seed candidates: n-Category Café, Math3ma (Tai-Danae Bradley), John Baez (Azimuth + n-cat), Bartosz Milewski, Andrej Bauer, Conal Elliott, Jacques Carette.
arXiv — TBD. Likely cs.LO, cs.PL, math.CT, with an author-based filter later if volume is too high.
YouTube — TBD. Channel feeds for lecture / conference channels: POPL, OPLSS, Topos Institute, etc. (Same endpoint as the playlist trick — verify it isn't broadly blocked before investing time.)
Mastodon — TBD. Per-user feeds of the form https://INSTANCE/@user.rss for people whose posts warrant a read-later signal rather than in-client following.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Quirk discovered during setup: the FreshRSS main-UI "Actualize feeds" button respects per-feed cache TTL and may skip a recently-added feed; Settings → Subscription management → Refresh forces a full re-fetch and is the right way to verify a newly-added feed is fetching correctly.

Undecided: Reddit via RSS. Most subreddits support /.rss, but the signal-to-noise of even filtered subs is usually worse than HN/Lobsters for the same time budget. Revisit if a specific subreddit proves worth it.
Organization principle: Queue first (curated by me), then high-signal news, then blogs and arXiv (research input), then video and social last. FreshRSS respects category order in NetNewsWire.
Self-hosted FreshRSS on macproseph (port 8090, Tailscale-only). Client: NetNewsWire on iOS, connected via GReader API at http://100.83.148.105:8090/api/greader.php.
